title: Edge fill & cold-warm priming brief — 2026-11-24
content:
Purpose: capture the conversation from the 11/24 priming sync — testing a cold->warm priming pattern for edge regions to reduce percent of high-latency cold starts during short customer spikes. Not a rollout doc; mostly hypothesis, short experiments, and immediate actions.

Summary:
- Problem: 3–7% of user requests in low-volume edge regions hit cold workers and show >600ms additional per-request latency. For latency-sensitive enterprise customers this produces SLO violations during bursty usage.
- Hypothesis: A small pool of warm-but-idle nodes (warm workers with KV cache pre-loaded and lightweight model initialization) plus a limited cold-node burn-in routine will reduce tail latency without incurring the cost of full dedicated capacity.
- Early metric target: reduce 95th pct latency delta from warm baseline by 50% for edge regions during 5–30 minute spikes.

Observed baseline (last 14 days):
- us-west-edge: avg spare GPUs 14, cold-start rate ~5.8%, 95th delta +620ms
- eu-west-edge: avg spare GPUs 9, cold-start rate ~4.1%, 95th delta +480ms
- ap-south-edge: avg spare GPUs 4, cold-start rate ~6.9%, 95th delta +720ms
- daily churn (node preemptions/reboots) across all edge regions: ~6.4%

Experiment plan (WIP):
1) Warm pool sizing pilot (2 weeks):
   - Create 1.2x baseline warm pool in us-west-edge (target warm GPUs = 18).
   - Policy: warm nodes kept at low-utilization (<10% of throughput) and pinned to high-priority customer routes.
   - Measurement: tail latency by customer tier, KV cache hit rate, cost delta.

2) Cold burn-in cadence (A/B):
   - A: periodic short burn-in where a cold node is exercised with synthetic tiny requests (10–30s) to populate JIT, kernels, and KV priming; runs every 4 hours.
   - B: on-demand burn-in triggered when prefix-hit drops below threshold or when a surge is detected by signal.
   - Goal: determine cost vs. efficacy tradeoffs.

3) Eviction & fallback rules refinement:
   - Adjust eviction heuristic to prefer preemptible->cold eviction first, keep warm pool intact for the next 30 minutes after a surge.
   - Route low-priority background workloads to dedicated preemptible pool to preserve warm capacity.

Immediate actions from sync: (owners and rough ETA)
- Put warm-pool pilot into terraform for us-west-edge; 48h rollback window. Owner: Mateo Ruiz. ETA: 2026-11-26.
- Add synthetic burn-in script to priming repo; instrument for KV cache warmness gauge. Owner: Jinsoo Kim. ETA: 2026-11-27.
- Dashboard: add new tile showing warm-pool occupancy, synthetic-burn-in success rate, and 95th delta per region. Owner: Leah Thompson. ETA: 2026-11-30.
- Update routing policy RFC draft to include warm-pool route pins and eviction hierarchy. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-12-03.

Risks & notes:
- Cost: expected incremental cost for warm pools ~+6–12% infra spend in pilot region; budget approval required if we scale.
- Correctness: synthetic burn-in must not pollute user telemetry or inadvertently train any logs; ensure burn-in is explicitly marked and excluded from evals.
- Failure modes: warm pool fragmentation if autoscaler mis-sizes groups; need autoscaler gating to ensure warm nodes are stable for min 5 minutes.

Metrics to track (weekly cadence):
- Cold-start rate (per region)
- 95th latency delta (cold vs warm baseline)
- Warm pool cost delta (USD/day)
- KV cache hit rate after burn-in
- Synthetic burn-in success rate

Notes for oncall / runbook additions:
- If warm pool causes sustained underutilization (>40% idle for 6h) we scale down by 25% and notify infra-capacity channel.
- If burn-in scripts fail 3x in a row -> auto-disable pilot and page infra-eng oncall.

Links & references:
- INFRA-3421: priming strategy backlog (Jira)
- priming-scripts repo: PR #12 (initial burn-in script)
- previous regional fill notes: see slack thread #edge-capacity-nov

Open questions (needs follow-up in next sync):
- Should warm pools be tenant-aware (per-large-customer) or pooled across all high-priority routes? Pros/cons to model cache contamination and security.
- Acceptable cost delta for enterprise customers to enable guaranteed warm routing? Who signs off?

Quick log of meeting attendees and short comments:
- Aisha: framing and RFC timeline.
- Mateo: prefers conservative warm pool sizing, wants rollback hooks.
- Jinsoo: wants more telemetry before enabling burn-in in eu-west.
- Leah: will wire up dashboards and add cost visualization.

Next sync: 2026-12-01 09:00 PT — focus on pilot telemetry and any immediate anomalies from initial warm pool rollout.

Raw checklist (copy for runbook):
- [ ] Terraform change checkin for us-west-edge warm pool
- [ ] Burn-in script merged + instrumentation
- [ ] Dashboard tiles created
- [ ] RFC updated with eviction policy
- [ ] Cost approval request drafted for scaling beyond pilot

End of brief.
